### 📓 Docs Drift Check

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `97c06b6df7439abf9fa4e898e6a3a63526e64aeb` — the merge of head `236748846a49323b9223904672f1a0c049a7cb32` into base `b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 97c06b6df7439abf9fa4e898e6a3a63526e64aeb && git checkout 97c06b6df7439abf9fa4e898e6a3a63526e64aeb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b85dff0f4350f4846b03c31b328fc5a8f782d1c9
```

Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c (epic #34659)

### 席位核对
- Card #35025, `Fixes #35025` in the body. 17 files, +562/−37, all under `packages/qa/scenarios/**`, `docs/qa/scenarios/**` and one changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 35044`: NOT governed (0 of 17 paths), under the size threshold.
- CI on c8ab4e48: 37 success, 18 skipped, nothing red or pending.
- Round 2 = the round-1 fix (6513b37c) + a plain merge of main eb7b09d4 (a856f36a) + the card stamp (5a802de5) + docs (c8ab4e48). No earlier L1 on this PR, so this is a full read of the whole diff against main.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/scenarios` patch, `Metadata-protocol: none`, so patch is the right level. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` lists the new record/scorecard members (`card`, `cardStamp`), the optional post-state members (`sum`, `each`, relation-path `where` keys), the new exports (`CardStamp`, `cardStampOf`, `cardStampText`, `relationObjects`, `DeclaredLookups`) and the summary dimension. I checked that list against the diff and it is complete. Every widening is additive: old cards still parse (`values` / `absent` unchanged), old records still sum with each other (`card: not recorded`).

### What I checked
- **Schema** (`schema.ts`): an entry carries exactly one of `values`, `absent` or an aggregate. An aggregate is named by `where` and never by `id`. `sum` / `each` must name at least one field. `where` keys widen to `FieldPathSchema`, and `values` / `sum` / `each` keys stay `MachineNameSchema`, which is right because they are the object's own fields.
- **Loader** (`loader.ts`): `where` keys go through `checkPath`, which already resolves relation paths through declared lookups. `values` / `sum` / `each` fields go through `checkField`. A summed field that holds a non-number on any seed row is refused.
- **Grading** (`aggregateChecks`): no matched row gives one failing `->rows` check, so a sum of nothing never passes as 0 and a vacuous "every row" never passes. A row reading no number fails `.sum(field)` with the offending cells named. The sum tolerance is 1e-6 and `each` compares with the same `same()` as `values`. The aggregate branch returns before the "exactly one row" duplicate check, which is correct: many rows is what an aggregate reads.
- **Relation paths** (`observe.ts`): `relationObjects` walks every hop but the last through `expect.lookups`, and orchestrate reads those objects after the turn beside the post-states' own. `readPath` follows string ids only. An unresolved hop reads `undefined`, which matches only a declared `null`. Path keys skip the card's-today leniency, which is right because that leniency is about a field stamped on this row. `touchedRowId` gets the lookups too, so the audit-actor read on a `where`-named row still resolves.
- **The card change**: `claim.trip` → `claim_line.claim` (→ `expense_claim`) → `.trip`. All three lookups are declared in `expect.lookups`. No seeded `expense_claim` sits on `t121` (the seed has only the trip row), so the sums read only the lines of the claim the turn created. A duplicate claim for t121 would double the sums and fail, which is the right verdict. The claim-level entry (claimant e02, `submitted`, `total_amount` 1205, `auditActor`) is unchanged.
- **The card stamp**: `cardStampOf` hashes the card file's bytes. `runRecord` puts it at the top level and on the scorecard. The scorecard prints `card: <id> (sha256 <12>)` under the packages line. `summary` adds `card` to `TABLE_DIMENSIONS`. Two hashes, or a stamped record next to an unstamped one, refuse the table. Unstamped records keep their old dimensions line.
- **Tests** cover:
  - quantity-2/3 lines versus per-night/per-day lines;
  - the seed's other lines and another new claim left out;
  - the recorded run still failing on status alone;
  - a short night, an over-standard line and an empty claim all failing;
  - missing lookups failing rather than summing every hotel line;
  - decimals;
  - no row matched;
  - the three summary refusal and accept cases;
  - the loader control.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: `cli.ts` takes the stamp with `readFileSync(loaded.file)` after `runCard` returns. So it hashes the file as it is when the record is written, not the bytes the run loaded, which is what the `CardStamp` doc comment and the changeset say. In practice it only differs if the card is edited during a run. Either read the bytes once at load time and carry them, or reword the doc to "as the file reads when the record is written". Not blocking.
- N2: c4a0c6d8 has a `wip(...)` subject. The squash on landing covers it. Keep the squash title as the fix line.

### Next
Clause-② is yes, so this goes to the seat's L2. After that it is an ordinary queue landing (not governed). If anything is pushed after c8ab4e48, a delta read is owed.

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and changeset; 0 of 17 paths published-schema or governed). Inputs read: card #35025 body and all 4 comments (claim 6964093785, round-1 report 6964789623, claim amendment 6966396612, round-2 report 6966433661); PR #35044 body, 17-file list, net diff `eb7b09d4..c8ab4e48`; PR comments (docs-drift 6964796696, L1 ACCEPT 6966499629, this review's claim 6966524337); check-runs on the head.

Success includes Lint & Repo Gates (all 8 scoped legs), TypeScript Type Check (4 legs), Test Core (planned shards 1-7 and the aggregate), Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset (all 3 runs; the last finished 01:49:18Z), PR-body guards (3 runs), Check Documentation Links. The rest are skipped by path filter.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies (`./runner` re-exports `observe`, `scorecard` and `summary`; `.` re-exports `schema` and `loader`; the card library ships as package data):

1. **`PostStateSchema` gains optional `sum` and `each`. Right, widening.** The exactly-one refine now counts `values`, `absent` and an aggregate. For a card without an aggregate it is the old `values` xor `absent` rule, so every old card still parses. The new refusals (an aggregate by `id`, an empty `sum`/`each`) only reach the new members.
2. **`where` keys go from `MachineNameSchema` to `FieldPathSchema`. Right, widening.** The `FieldPathSchema` regex accepts every machine name, since a path with no dot is a machine name. In the loader, `checkPath` on a dotless key falls straight through to `checkField`, the check `where` keys had before (`loader.ts` 662-679), so no old card is newly refused.
3. **The loader refuses a `sum` field that holds a non-number on a seed row. Right.** It applies only to the new member.
4. **Grader `aggregateChecks` (`scenario-operation-grade.ts`). Right.** Zero matched rows fail `->rows` once, so a sum or each over nothing is never vacuously met. A cell that is not a number fails `.sum(field)` and names the offending cells. The tolerance is 1e-6. `each` compares with the same `same()` as `values`. The branch returns before the one-row duplicate check, which is the point of an aggregate. Old entries never take the branch.
5. **Relation paths in `observe.ts` (`relationObjects`, `readPath`, `matches`). Right.** Every hop but the last goes through `expect.lookups`, a hop reads only a string id, and an unresolved hop reads `undefined`, which matches nothing but a declared `null`. Path keys skip the card's-today leniency, which is about a field stamped on the row itself. `postStateRows`, `touchedRowId` and `ObserveInput` each gain one optional trailing member that defaults to no lookups, so existing callers are unchanged.
6. **The card change (`travel_expense.json`, `file_and_submit_from_text`). Right, and it is what #35025 asks for.** Hotel `sum(amount)=860` and meals `sum(amount)=345` are scoped through `claim.trip = t121`, plus `each(over_standard)=false` over every line of that claim. The hop chain `claim_line.claim` to `expense_claim`, then `.trip`, is declared in the card's `expect.lookups` (read on the head). The claim-level entry and `auditActor` are unchanged. This loosens the line-shape pin by design: unit amount and quantity are no longer checked, and the per-type totals are. A duplicate claim on t121 doubles the sums and fails, which is the right verdict.
7. **Record top-level `card: {id, sha256}`, scorecard `cardStamp`, and the scorecard line. Right as a shape, widening.** All are optional and absent when no stamp is passed (`runRecord`, `cardScorecard`). No existing record or scorecard field is removed, renamed or made required. The provenance of the hash is wrong in one window, see S1 in ③.
8. **`summary` gains a `card` dimension (`TABLE_DIMENSIONS`). Right: it does not narrow stored records.** A record without `card` reads `card: not recorded`. Every pre-change record reads that same value, so stored records keep summing with each other, and their dimensions line is unchanged because `NO_CARD_STAMP` is filtered out (`summary.ts` 495). The only newly refused table mixes a pre-change record with a stamped one. A stamped record could not exist before this change, so no input set that summed before is refused now. The refusal names both sides and their files, as claimed: the generic dimension refusal (`summary.ts` 437-441) prints `` the runs differ in card: `card: ID (sha256 FIRST12)` (files) vs `card: ID (sha256 FIRST12)` (files) ``. It is pinned verbatim in `summary.test.ts`, both for two hashes (a1, a2 vs b, exit 1) and for stamped vs `not recorded`. The "hash" it names is the 12-hex prefix; the full sha256 stays in the record (see n1).
9. **New exports `CardStamp`, `cardStampOf`, `cardStampText`, `relationObjects`, `DeclaredLookups`. Additive, and the Clause-② line lists all five.** The list is complete against the diff.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. **Right.** By AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3), the level follows the Metadata-protocol kind alone, and `none` takes patch. `none` is right because the scenario-card format is a devx instrument, not platform metadata (the package description says "packages/spec carries no obligation for this format"), so no metadata author's accept-set moves. The `(widening)` arm is right by ① 1-9. Check Changeset is green on all three runs.
- `Clause-②:` the `yes (widening)` line is present at line start in both the PR body and the changeset, and matches the claim amendment 6966396612. The round-1 claim's `Clause-②: no` was superseded by that amendment when the stamp was added.
- One sentence in the changeset is not true in every case: "the sha256 of the card file's bytes as the runner loaded them". That changeset ships as CHANGELOG text, so it is folded into S1 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

**S1 (should-fix): the card stamp hashes the file at record-write time, not the bytes the run loaded. This is L1 N1, graded up from a note.**
- What the code does: `cli.ts` 485 calls `cardStampOf(loaded.card.id, readFileSync(loaded.file))` after `await runCard(...)` returns. The loader read and parsed the card at startup (`loader.ts` 208, `loadOne`), before the per-card loop.
- What the contract says: "the card file's bytes as the runner loaded them" in the `CardStamp` jsdoc, the `cli.ts` comment, both READMEs and the changeset.
- **Wrong hash.** If the card is edited between load and write, the record and scorecard stamp bytes the run never graded. That is plausible in a working tree, since a round runs builds, asks and repeats for a long time. On a multi-card run, the window for card N covers the whole run of cards 1 to N-1. `summary` would then sum that record with post-edit rounds, which is the silent mix this PR exists to refuse.
- **Lost record.** If the card file is renamed, removed or switched away (for example a branch checkout) mid-run, `readFileSync` throws after the run, before `writeFileSync`. The whole run's record is lost, and so are the remaining cards'.
- The file already has the right pattern: the supplied template is hashed from the same `templateBytes` it parses (`cli.ts` 457-460).
- Fix: carry the loaded bytes, or their sha256, on `LoadedScenario` from `loadOne`, and stamp from that. Rewording the docs alone fixes the wording but leaves the record-loss path.
- No grade changes either way. A delta read is owed on the fixing head.

**n1 (nit):** `summary` compares the card dimension on `cardStampText`, which is the 12-hex prefix, not the full sha256. Two distinct card hashes that share a 48-bit prefix would sum. That is negligible, and the record keeps the full hash. Comparing on `r.card.sha256` and printing the prefix would make it exact.

**n2 (nit):** Adding `'card'` to the exported `TABLE_DIMENSIONS` tuple makes the exported `SummaryTable.dims: Record of TableDimension to string` require a `card` key.
- Who it affects: a consumer that builds its own `SummaryTable` to pass to the exported `renderSummaryTable`. For that consumer it is a compile-time tightening of an input type on the `./runner` subpath.
- Why it stays a nit, not a narrowing: no in-repo producer exists besides `summaryTables`, and no stored data is affected. #34808 added `'ask skills'` to the same tuple the same way and shipped it as widening. Recorded as an accepted deviation, not a narrowing.

**n3 (nit, L1 N2 carried):** c4a0c6d8 has a `wip(...)` subject. The squash on landing covers it.

**SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding.**
- The new code does an in-app join: `readPath` over a second `listRows` (`expense_claim`), next to the existing per-post-state `listRows`.
- This builds no query capability. It is the eval runner observing a throwaway app from outside, through the public data API. It grades the rows the API reads back, and applies the card's-today leniency in-app on the same read. The diff states this as its reason ("read through the rows the data API returns after the turn", `schema.ts` and `observe.ts` jsdoc), the same shape as every existing post-state read.
- One limit, outside the diff and inherited: `listRows` caps at `limit=1000`. A hop object over that cap fails a match (an unresolved hop reads `undefined`), never passes one falsely.

**Dev flags and `open_questions`:**
- **Open question, carried in both reports: may the dev-written PR body carry the `signed:` HTML comment line?**
  - Escalated to the seat. It is a rule-text conflict, not a contract matter.
  - The two texts that conflict: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/seat-post-protocol.md` line 30 requires the last line of the PR body to be the `signed:` comment, and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` lines 319-320 ban HTML comments written by the dev (the only exception is the harness's attribution first line).
  - Provisional answer: option A holds for this head. The signed line is intact on read-back as the last line of the PR body. It does not affect the verdict.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`RecordedDriver.createdIdOf` reads only a top-level `id`, so a `run_action` replay is not faithful):** outside this diff and on #35064's surface. The seat files or confirms it. Not this PR's to fix.
- **L1 notes:** N1 is graded up to S1 above. N2 is applied as a title patch and carried as n3.
- **PR author:** `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so there is no off-relay author to name.
- **Round-1 carry (per-type sums card and grader):** reviewed in full as ① 1-6. No must-fix.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: S1 (open; a delta read is owed before landing, per contract-review.md: "no open must-fix or should-fix").

## Contract review

This is a delta review of `c8ab4e48..b2d22c5f` on top of the PASS record at `c8ab4e48`, which carried S1.

**Face: declaration.** The delta adds no path. It is one fast-forward commit (b2d22c5f) touching 6 files that are already in the PR's 17-file list. None of them is a published schema or a governed path. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on both the PR body and the changeset.

**Inputs read:**
- Card #35025: the body and all 5 comments, including the round-3 report 6967245666 (`open_questions: []`).
- PR #35044: the body (patched in round 3), the 17-file list, the delta diff, and the comments up to the L1 delta ACCEPT 6967272630.
- The check-runs on the head.

**Check-runs on `b2d22c5f`:**
- 55 runs, all completed: 37 success, 18 skipped by path filter, none failed, cancelled or timed out.
- The 37 successes include:
  - Lint & Repo Gates and all 8 scoped legs
  - TypeScript Type Check and its 4 legs
  - Test Core: all 7 planned shards and the aggregate
  - Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard

  - PR-body guards: both runs, the last finished 02:32:24Z
  - Check Documentation Links
- The L1 read saw one run still in progress. That run has since finished green.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **S1 is closed: the card stamp now hashes the exact bytes that were parsed.**
   - In `loader.ts` `loadOne`, one `readFileSync(file)` returns a Buffer. `createHash('sha256')` over that Buffer becomes `fileSha256`, and `JSON.parse(bytes.toString('utf8'))` parses the same Buffer.
   - Nothing normalises the bytes between the hash and the parse. `Buffer#toString('utf8')` decodes exactly as the old `readFileSync(file, 'utf8')` did. Neither strips a BOM, so a BOM-led card is refused as not valid JSON, the same as before.
   - The algorithm is the one `cardStampOf` uses (`scorecard.ts` 300: sha256 hex over the same bytes), so a stamp taken either way agrees.
   - A read error (ENOENT, EISDIR) still lands in the existing catch as the same `not valid JSON` refusal. A loaded card therefore always carries the field, and TS definite assignment holds: the catch returns, and Type Check is green.
2. **No path re-reads the card after loading.**
   - `cli.ts` 495 now calls `loadedCardStamp(loaded)`, which builds `{ id: loaded.card.id, sha256: loaded.fileSha256 }`. Its result feeds both `runRecord` (496) and `cardScorecard` (499). These are the only two stamp consumers in `src/`, since `runRecord` and `cardScorecard` have no other callers.
   - **Multi-card runs.** `loadScenarios` hashes every card before the `for (const loaded of chosen)` loop, so card N's stamp no longer depends on how long cards 1 to N-1 ran.
   - **`--iterate`.** `iteratedScenario` (`orchestrate.ts` 615) works on the rebased `scenario`, never on the stamp.
